title: God Is Our Refuge and Defence
description: God Is Our Refuge and Defence in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 634 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God is our re-fuge and de-fence, In trou-ble our un-fail-ing aid; Se-cure in his om-ni-po-tence, What foe can make our soul a-fraid?

lines: God is our refuge and defence,
What foe can make our soul afraid?
Yea, though the earth's foundations rock,
And mountains down the gulf be hurled,
His people smile amid the shock,
They look beyond this transient world.
There is a river pure and bright,
Whose streams make glad the heavenly plains,
The city of our God remains.
Built by the word of his command,
Firm as his throne the bulwarks stand;
There is our home, our hope, our rest.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
